text.p: Mobil Corp said Wednesday a significant natural gas and condensate discovery has been made in Norwegian Petroleum License 199 (Block 6406/2) southwest of the Aasgard Unit in the Norwegian Sea.
Mobil said it has a 15 percent interest in the discovery, which will be called "Kristin," the second in License 199 which further strengthens the probability of commercial development.
It said the operator of the license, Saga Petroleum A/S, encountered natural gas and condensate in two formations of the wildcat well, 6406/2-3.
The discovery well reached a depth of 5,258 meters below sea level in formations of Lower Jurassic Age.
Mobil said the combined rate for the two formations was 58 million cubic feet of natural gas and 11,500 barrels of condensate per day.
It said Saga has a 25 percent stake in the find, while Statoil owns 15 percent and the state's direct financial interest is 45 percent.

The first discovery, named "Lavrans," was made in late 1995 on a separate structure, Mobil said. That find is ranked by the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate as the largest on the Norwegian Continental Shelf in the last ten years.
This "Kristin" discovery appears to be as large, or larger than "Lavrans," but with a higher liquids content, Mobil said.
Possible natural gas transportation alternatives for "Kristin" and "Lavrans" include a tie-in to the Aasgard field system or a separate export pipeline, if sufficient volumes are proven in the area.
Mobil said the large volumes discovered so far on the license suggest a stand-alone development as the most likely development scenario. Earliest production is expected in 2001.
